note: Authored pack: s17 (NumPy) carries theory/coding/debug/logic, s18 (Pandas) carries interview/solved/checkpoint/defense — 20 each across the track.

items.q: ndarray list se kya behtar deta hai?
items.a: Fixed dtype (homogeneous), contiguous memory aur vectorized C-level operations — isliye 10-100x fast arithmetic aur kam memory overhead. Trade-off: ek array me ek hi dtype, mixed types ke liye list/dict.

items.q: shape aur dtype ka kya role hai?
items.a: shape har axis ka length batata hai (rows, cols), dtype element ka type aur size (int64, float32). Operations inhi do par validate hote hain — broadcasting aur memory dono inhi se decide hote hain.

items.q: NumPy broadcasting ke rules teen points me likho.
items.a: 1) Right se align karo. 2) Dimensions equal ya ek side 1 ho to stretch hoga. 3) Mismatch par ValueError. Broadcasting copy nahi banata — view se compute hota hai.

items.q: Slicing view deti hai ya copy — aur uska bug kya hai?
items.a: Basic slicing view deti hai (same buffer), isliye slice me change karne par original badal jaata hai. Fancy/boolean indexing copy deta hai. Fix: .copy() explicitly jab independent array chahiye.

items.q: axis parameter ka matlab kya hai (sum(axis=0) vs axis=1)?
items.a: axis woh dimension hai jo collapse hoti hai: 2D me axis=0 columns ke across (per-column, output me rows khatam), axis=1 rows ke across (per-row, output me columns khatam).
items.x: Axis = jo collapse ho raha hai.

items.q: Vectorization loop se kyun tez hai?
items.a: Loop Python interpreter me per-element kaam karta hai (object boxing + type checks), jabki vectorized ops C loops me chalti hain aur SIMD use karti hain. Isliye rule: loop likhne se pehle vectorized alternative dhundo.

items.q: Boolean mask indexing kaise kaam karta hai?
items.a: arr[arr > 5] ek boolean array se filter karta hai aur copy return karta hai. Combine ke liye & | ke saath parentheses lagana zaroori hai, kyunki comparison operators ki precedence zyada hoti hai.

items.q: reshape aur resize me farq batao.
items.a: reshape view/na utna memory share karke naya shape deta hai (elements total same hone chahiye), resize original array ko in-place badalta hai (size badha bhi sakta hai). Data safe rakho to reshape.

items.q: hstack/vstack aur concatenate me choice kaise karte hain?
items.a: Rows jodne ke liye concatenate([a, b], axis=0) ya vstack, columns ke liye axis=1 ya hstack. Explicit axis wala concatenate sabse clear hai aur dimension mismatch par saaf error deta hai.

items.q: Random seed set karna testing me kyun zaroori hai?
items.a: Reproducibility ke liye: default_rng(42) se same data har run me milta hai, isliye tests stable rehte hain. Production me alag seeds use karo par test fixtures me fixed.

items.q: NumPy me NaN handle karne ke kaunse tools hain?
items.a: np.isnan se detect, np.nanmean/np.nansum se skip karke aggregate, np.nan_to_num se replace. Dhyan: NaN ke saath koi bhi comparison False hota hai, isliye == nahi, isnan use karo.

items.q: Vectorized ops me float precision ka dhyan kyun rakhna chahiye?
items.a: Float64 me bhi 0.1 exact nahi hota, isliye == comparison fail karta hai. Fixed-point/cents me paisa rakho, aur comparison ke liye np.isclose(rtol=..., atol=...) use karo.

items.q: dtype casting ke rules kya hain (int + float, int8 overflow)?
items.a: Mixed ops me safe/common type choose hota hai (int64 + float64 → float64). Fixed-width int overflow wrap kar jaata hai (int8 127+1 = -128), isliye large numbers ke liye int64/float use karo.

items.q: In-place operators (+=, *=) ka fayda aur khatra kya hai?
items.a: Memory bachate hain (naya array nahi banta) aur cache-friendly hote hain; khatra ye hai ki dtype mismatch par error aata hai aur view/shared buffer use ho sakta hai — 'a += 1' ne aisa bug banaya jo 'a = a + 1' me nahi tha.
items.x: Memory bachta hai, dtype sharp rehta hai.

items.q: Aggregate ke saath nan handling kaise karte hain (mean example)?
items.a: np.nanmean(x) NaN skip karke mean deta hai (np.mean nan deta hai). Ya pehle mask se NaN hatao: x[~np.isnan(x)]. Which is right depends: silently skip karna metric ko optimistic bana sakta hai — count bhi report karo.
items.x: Skip karo par count bhi dikhao.

items.q: Memory layout (C order vs F order) aur performance ka rishta kya hai?
items.a: C order row-major hai, isliye row direction me iterate karna cache-friendly hota hai (F order column-major). Bade arrays me layout mismatch random access dega aur speed chali jaayegi — np.ascontiguousarray se fix karo.
items.x: Access pattern layout se match karao.

items.q: dot/matmul aur elementwise * me farq batao.
items.a: * elementwise multiply karta hai (shape mismatch par broadcast/error), @ ya np.matmul matrix product karta hai ((m,k)@(k,n) → (m,n)). Machine learning code me yahi sabse common confusion hai.

items.q: Bade arrays me memory blow-up se kaise bachte ho?
items.a: Views/slices use karo, in-place ops, float32 instead of float64, chunk/batch processing, aur output ko preallocate karo. Kabhi-kabhi ek expression (a - b) ** 2 do temporary arrays banata hai — isliye steps me likho aur del karo.

items.q: np.where ka use-case batao.
items.a: Conditional selection: np.where(cond, a, b) vectorized if-else hai — jaise negative values ko 0 karna, ya grade assign karna. Nested conditions ke liye np.select zyada readable hai.

items.q: NumPy me 1D array banao 0..9 ka, usme se even numbers filter karo aur unka sum nikalo.
items.a:
import numpy as np

a = np.arange(10)
evens = a[a % 2 == 0]
print(evens, evens.sum())

items.q: Ek 2D array ka per-row mean nikalo (float me).
items.a:
import numpy as np

m = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
print(m.mean(axis=1))

items.q: Array ko min-max normalize karo (0-1 range).
Bade array ka max aur uska index nikalo.
items.a:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([3, 9, 4, 9])
print(x.max(), x.argmax())
# saare ties chahiye to: np.flatnonzero(x == x.max())
items.x: argmax pehla max deta hai, ties sab chahiye to flatnonzero.

items.q: Do arrays compress/stack karke (N, 2) matrix banao.
items.a:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([1, 2, 3]); y = np.array([4, 5, 6])
print(np.column_stack([x, y]))
print(np.stack([x, y], axis=1))
items.x: column_stack columns ke roop me jodta hai.

items.q: Matrix multiply karo two matrices ka, aur shape verify karo.

A = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
B = np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)
C = A @ B
print(C.shape, C[0, 0])

items.q: Array ka unique values aur unke counts nikalo.
items.a:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3])
values, counts = np.unique(x, return_counts=True)

items.q: NaN values ko 0 se replace karo aur kitne replace hue woh batao.
items.a:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0, np.nan])
mask = np.isnan(x)
print(int(mask.sum()))
x = np.where(mask, 0.0, x)
items.x: Count lo, phir replace karo — audit trail.

items.q: Array ko fixed range me clip karo (-1 se 1).
items.a:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([-3.0, 0.5, 4.0])
print(np.clip(x, -1.0, 1.0))
items.x: clip outliers ko boundary par le aata hai.

items.q: Moving average nikalo np.convolve se (window 3).
items.a:
import numpy as np

x = np.arange(10, dtype=float)
w = np.ones(3) / 3
ma = np.convolve(x, w, mode='valid')
print(ma)
items.x: valid mode se output chhota aur clean hota hai.

items.q: Integer labels ko one-hot matrix me convert karo (numpy only).
items.a:
import numpy as np

def one_hot(labels, num_classes=None):
    labels = np.asarray(labels)
    n = num_classes or (labels.max() + 1)
    out = np.zeros((labels.size, n), dtype=int)
    out[np.arange(labels.size), labels] = 1
    return out
items.x: Advanced indexing se ek line me set hota hai.

items.q: Bade array ko batches me slice karo aur har batch ka sum do.
items.x: Slicing vectorized rakhne se per-batch kaam sasta.

items.q: Two 1D vectors ka dot product teen tarike se nikalo.
items.a:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3]); b = np.array([4, 5, 6])
print(a @ b, np.dot(a, b), (a * b).sum())
items.x: Teeno same result — clarity ke liye @ prefer karo.

items.q: 2D array ka per-row maximum nikalo.
items.a:
import numpy as np

m = np.array([[1, 7, 3], [4, 2, 9]])
print(m.max(axis=1))
print(m.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))
items.x: keepdims broadcasting ke liye useful hai.

items.q: Matrix ke har row ka top-2 index nikalo (sort ke bina poori ordering).
items.a:
import numpy as np

m = np.array([[1, 7, 3], [4, 2, 9]])
idx = np.argsort(m, axis=1)[:, -2:][:, ::-1]
print(idx)

items.q: Do arrays ka elementwise safe division karo (zero par 0).
items.a:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1.0, 2.0]); b = np.array([0.0, 2.0])
with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
    out = np.divide(a, b, out=np.zeros_like(a), where=b != 0)
items.x: where= mask se zero-division warning bhi nahi.

items.q: Array ke values ko percentile rank me convert karo (0-100).
items.x: argsort ke argsort se rank milta hai.

items.q: Sparse labels ke liye class weights nikalo (inverse frequency).
items.a:
import numpy as np

labels = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2])
values, counts = np.unique(labels, return_counts=True)
weights = (counts.sum() / (len(values) * counts))
print(dict(zip(values.tolist(), np.round(weights, 3).tolist())))
items.x: Rare class ko zyada weight — imbalance ka basic fix.

items.q: (3,1) aur (1,4) arrays ka sum ka shape kya hoga?
items.a: (3, 4) — dono size-1 dimensions stretch hote hain (broadcast). Agar dono axes me size >1 aur unequal hoti to ValueError aata.

items.q: print(np.array([1, 2, 3]) / 2) aur print(np.array([1, 2, 3]) // 2) ke output batao.
items.a: Pehla [0.5, 1, 1.5] (true division float deta hai), doosra [0, 1, 1] (floor division). Integer array me // silently truncate karta hai — percentage nikalte waqt yahi bug aata hai.

items.q: x = np.arange(5); y = x[:3]; y[0] = 99; print(x[0]) — output?
items.a: 99 — slicing view deti hai, isliye y me change original x me dikhta hai. Independent copy ke liye y = x[:3].copy().

items.q: np.array([True, True, False]).sum() kya deta hai?
items.a: 2 — booleans ko 0/1 maan kar sum hota hai (bina explicit cast ke). Isliye 'kitne pass hue' jaisa count mask.sum() se ek line me nikalta hai.

items.q: x = np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype=np.int8); x[0] += 200; print(x[0]) — output?
items.a: Overflow wrap hota hai: 201 mod 256 = -55 (int8 range −128..127). Isliye currency/counters ke liye int64 ya float, aur range check input par karo.

items.q: print(np.nan == np.nan) — output aur uska practical asar?
items.a: False — NaN kisi ke bhi barabar nahi hota (khud ke bhi nahi). Isliye NaN ko dedupe/filter karne ke liye == use na karo; isnan() ya pandas ke special handling use karo.

items.q: A shape (5,3) hai aur B shape (5,) — A * B ka output shape kya hoga?
items.a: (5, 3) — B right-align hokar (1,5) ban jaata hai, phir broadcasting (5,3) vs (5,) FAIL karta hai... sahi jawab: ye ValueError deta hai, kyunki trailing dims 3 vs 5 mismatch hain. Sahi intent ke liye B[:, None] se (5,1) banao.
items.x: Trailing dims align hote hain — yahan mismatch.

items.q: np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3) aur .reshape(3, 2) me element order kaise badalta hai?
items.a: Default C order me flatten hota hai (row-major), isliye reshape se same 1D sequence dobara groupped hoti hai — values wahi rehti hain, sirf arrangement badalta hai. Column-wise chahiye to order='F' do.
items.x: Reshape data nahi badalta, arrangement badalta hai.

items.q: x = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3]); print(x.sum() == 0.6) — kya aayega?
items.a: False aayega (0.6000000000000001 jaisa value). Float precision ki wajah se equality fail hoti hai; np.isclose(x.sum(), 0.6) use karo.

items.q: arr[i] loop se vs arr.sum() — kis case me loop faster ho sakta hai?
items.a: Jab aapko har element par complex Python-level logic chalani ho (custom branching, dict lookups) — wahan Python loop hi hota hai. Pure arithmetic ke liye vectorized path almost always faster.
items.x: Vectorized arithmetic par loop nahi jeetega.

items.q: np.zeros((3,)) me 0.0 hai ya 0?
items.a: float64 ka 0.0 hai (zeros default float). Integer chahiye to dtype=int do — warna downstream me float dtype propagate hoti hai.

items.q: empty = np.empty(3); print(empty) — reliable hai?
items.a: Nahi — np.empty memory allocate karta hai par initialize nahi, isliye values garbage ho sakti hain (kabhi 0 dikh bhi sakta hai). Production me hamesha zeros/ones/full use karo.

items.q: 2D array ka mean(axis=0) aur mean() (bina axis) me kya farq hoga?
items.a: axis=0 per-column mean (length = columns) deta hai; bina axis poore array ka ek scalar mean deta hai. Aggregation ka output shape axis se hi decide hota hai.
items.x: Axis do to shape bachta hai, warna scalar.

items.q: print((np.array([1, 2]) + np.array([3, 4])).dtype) — int64 me?
items.a: int64 — same dtype wale ints ka result bhi int64 rehta hai. Float ke saath mixed karne par hi float me promote hota hai (int64 + float32 → float64).

items.q: arr = np.arange(6); view = arr.reshape(2, 3); view[0, 0] = 100; print(arr[0]) — output?
items.a: 100 — reshape ne view diya (data share), isliye mutation original me dikhta hai. Agar reshape possible nahi hota (non-contiguous), NumPy copy bana deta hai — isliye behaviour data par depend karta hai.
items.x: Reshape view de sakta hai, copy bhi.

items.q: arr.mean() ki jagah arr.sum() / arr.size likhne me kya risk hai?
items.a: NaN hone par mean() NaN deta hai (clear signal), par manual sum/size bhi NaN dega — asli risk: dtype. Integer array par sum() int overflow/size se galti deta hai aur size 0 par ZeroDivisionError. np.mean use karo.
items.x: Builtin aggregate edge cases handle karta hai.

items.q: Two arrays ka np.hstack([a, b]) 1D par kya karta hai?
items.a: Same as concatenate(axis=0) — 1D me horizontal/vertical ka farq nahi banta, isliye dono ek hi lamba vector dete hain. 2D me hstack columns jodta hai aur vstack rows.

items.q: np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 10, 3) ko dobara same seed se chalaya — same output?
items.a: Haan — Generator per-object state rakhta hai, isliye same seed se same sequence milti hai (reproducible). Legacy np.random.seed global state hai, isliye threaded tests me flaky ho sakta hai.

items.q: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,4) (3,) — fix kaise karoge?
items.a: Trailing dims mismatch hain (4 vs 3). Intent ke hisaab se b[:, None] se (3,1) banao ya axis specify karo — silently reshape karne se pehle data ka meaning verify karo.
items.x: Broadcast error = shape contract ka error.

items.q: Array ka mean NaN aa raha hai jabki data saaf dikhta hai. Pehla suspect?
items.a: Data me NaN ya inf hai (ya string se convert hote waqt fail hua). Fix: np.isnan(x).sum() se gino, phir np.nanmean ya imputation choose karo — silently skip karna metric badal deta hai.

items.q: arr[mask] me change karne par original array update nahi hua. Wajah?
items.a: Boolean/fancy indexing copy deta hai, isliye assignment original par asar nahi karta. Fix: original par mask assign karo (arr[mask] = value) ya arr[bool_mask] ke bajaye np.where use karo.
items.x: Mask copy banata hai, view nahi.

items.q: Percentage nikalte waqt sab values 0 aa rahi hain (counts integer hain). Fix?
items.a: Integer division ne truncate kar diya. Fix: numerator ko float me convert karo (100.0 * a / b) ya dtype=float array banao.

items.q: in-place '+=' float value ke saath int array par TypeError de raha hai. Fix?
items.a: In-place op dtype nahi badal sakta, isliye int array me 0.5 add nahi hoga. Fix: pehle x = x.astype(float) karo, ya out-of-place x = x + 0.5 likho.

items.q: Array update kiya par dusra array bhi badal gaya (unexpected). Root cause?
items.a: Dono naam ek hi buffer share kar rahe the (slicing/view ya shallow copy). Fix: boundary par .copy() explicit likho, aur mutation se pehle np.shares_memory(a, b) se check karo.

items.q: axis=0 aur axis=1 ulta lag gaya, probabilities ka sum 1 nahi aa raha. Fastest fix?
items.a: Shape assertion add karo: assert out.shape == (rows,), taaki axis ka mistake crash kare. Axis confusion ka permanent ilaaj explicit shape checks aur named shapes/constants hain.
items.x: Shape assert se axis bug pakdo.

items.q: np.array(data) ka dtype object aa gaya (float ops fail). Wajah?
items.a: Data me mixed types (strings + numbers, ya None) hain, isliye NumPy object dtype chun leta hai. Fix: input saaf karo (float(v) with error handling) aur explicit dtype=float64 pass karo.

items.q: DecisionThreshold: comparisons '==' se float columns par rarely match kar rahe hain. Fix?
items.a: Float equality unreliable hai — np.isclose(rtol=1e-9) ya rounding (np.round(x, 6)) use karo; ya paisa/percent ko integer units me store karo.

items.q: Training loop memory badhta ja raha hai, kuch tensors free nahi ho rahe. Kya karoge?
items.a: References hold karne wale structures (list me store, closure capture) check karo, del + gc.collect() se verify karo, aur in-place ops/preallocation use karo. tracemalloc se growth ka exact site nikalo.
items.x: Reference graph dekho, tracemalloc se confirm karo.

items.q: numpy random results run-to-run badal rahe hain (test flaky). Fix?
items.a: Global np.random ke bajaye explicit Generator with fixed seed use karo aur use function me pass karo (inject karo). Isse test deterministic aur production path independent rehta hai.
items.x: Seed inject karo, global state nahi.

items.q: Sorting ke baad original array ka order badal gaya (jo nahi chahiye tha). Fix?
items.a: np.sort naya array deta hai (original safe), par a.sort() in-place hai. Galti se in-place call hua to copy = a.copy() pehle, ya np.sort use karo.

items.q: Concatenate ke baad shape expected se alag aa gaya. Fastest diagnostic?
items.a: Har input ka .shape print karo aur expected (n, d) se compare karo — 90% cases me ek input 1D hai jise reshape/expand_dims chahiye. np.expand_dims(arr, 0) se fix hota hai.

items.q: Numeric drift: do tarike se sum kiya, results thode alag. Ye bug hai ya expected?
items.a: Expected hai — float addition order-se-sensitive hai (large + small me precision loss). Stable chahiye to Kahan summation ya pairwise/float128 use karo, aur tests me tolerance rakho (np.allclose).

items.q: Mask se delete kiya: x = np.delete(x, mask) — galat elements gaye. Wajah?
items.a: np.delete indices (ya boolean mask of same shape) expect karta hai, values nahi; boolean mask dene par woh positions delete karta hai. Sahi: x = x[~mask].
items.x: Delete positions leta hai, conditions nahi.

items.q: Bade array par stack banate waqt MemoryError aa gaya, par data chhota dikhta hai. Wajah?
items.a: Intermediate copies (broadcast results, dtype promotion to float64, list-vs-array conversion) memory multiply kar deti hain. Fix: dtype explicit rakho, in-place ops use karo aur chunk-wise process karo.

items.q: Performance: 1e7 elements par Python loop 30s le raha hai. Refactor kaise karoge?
items.a: Step 1: loop ko vectorized equivalent me likho (mask + np.where / arithmetic). Step 2: dtype float32/float64 check karo. Step 3: chunks me process karo agar memory tight hai. Measure karke bolo: loop 30s → vectorized 0.4s.

items.q: np.set_printoptions(threshold=...) ke bina bade array ka print output hi nahi dikh raha. Quick fix?
items.a: Threshold badhao (np.set_printoptions(threshold=1000, linewidth=120)) ya slice print karo (arr[:10]) — production me logging ke liye counts/stats print karo, poora array nahi.

items.q: Division ne RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide diya. Isko kaise handle karoge?
items.a: Warning ignore mat karo: np.errstate ke saath to out=np.zeros_like(a), where=b != 0 use karo, ya NaN ko explicitly detect karke report karo — silently suppress karna data quality ka signal chhupa deta hai.

items.q: Kaggle-style code me np.where ka output shape expected se alag hai. Wajah?
items.a: np.where(cond, a, b) me a/b broadcast hote hain — agar a scalar aur b column vector hai to result ka shape b se aata hai. Shapes explicitly likho aur result shape assert karo.

items.q: Interview: Series aur DataFrame me farq batao.
items.a: Series 1D labelled array hai (index + values), DataFrame 2D labelled structure hai (columns each ek Series). Series ke operations vectorized hote hain aur DataFrame columns ke saath align hote hain.

items.q: loc aur iloc me farq interview me kaise explain karoge?
items.a: loc label-based hai (inclusive slicing, index ke naam), iloc positional hai (Python-like, end exclusive). Confusion ka source yahi inclusive/exclusive farq hai, isliye explicit column lists ke saath likho.

items.q: groupby ke andar apply, agg aur transform me farq?
items.a: agg har group ko ek row summary deta hai, transform same-index result deta hai (original shape), apply arbitrary function chala kar kuch bhi return kar sakta hai. Row-level result chahiye to transform, summary chahiye to agg.

items.q: merge aur join me farq, aur merge ka validate parameter kyun useful hai?
items.a: merge columns/keys par flexible join deta hai (inner/left/right/outer), join index-based shortcut hai. validate='one_to_many'/'many_to_one' se accidental row explosion turant pakdi jaati hai.
items.x: Validate se silent duplicate explode pakdo.

items.q: Chained assignment warning ka matlab kya hai aur fix?
items.a: df[df.x > 0]['y'] = 1 ek temporary (copy) par likh raha hota hai, isliye asar nahi padta aur SettingWithCopyWarning aata hai. Fix: single-step loc: df.loc[df.x > 0, 'y'] = 1.
items.x: Loc me ek step me likho.

items.q: Apply se slow code ko kaise speed up karoge?
items.a: Pehle vectorized alternative dekho (arithmetic, np.where, str accessor, dt accessor), phir groupby transform/agg, aur bahut custom logic ho to numba/Cython ya chunks me C-level path. Measure: apply 8s → vectorized 0.2s.

items.q: Missing values ke saare tools batao (detect → decide → fix).
items.a: Detect: isna().sum(), missing pattern per column. Decide: drop (dropna) sirf tab jab missingness random ho; warna impute (median/mode/forward fill) ya indicator column add karo. Fix ke baad counts report karo.

items.q: Pivot aur pivot_table me farq?
items.a: pivot sirf unique index/column pairs par chalta hai (duplicates par error), pivot_table aggregate function leta hai (default mean) — isliye real data par pivot_table safer hai.

items.q: Datetime handling ke teen zaroori kaam likho.
items.a: Parse with errors='coerce', timezone-aware ya naive consistently rakho (mix mat karo), aur resample/rolling ke liye DatetimeIndex set karo. Saath me UTC me store karo aur display par local time.

items.q: Categorical dtype ka fayda kya hai?
items.a: Memory bachti hai (codes + levels) aur groupby/sort ka order explicit hota hai. Par categories ke bahar naya value NaN ban jaata hai, isliye mode/levels ko validate karo.
items.x: Memory + fixed order, par NaN risk.

items.q: Memory kam karne ke teen practical tarike likho.
items.a: Chhote dtypes (int8/int16, category), sirf zaroori columns load karo (usecols), aur chunked read (chunksize) — plus string columns ko category/string dtype me convert karna.

items.q: Copy-on-write (pandas 2.0+) ka practical asar kya hai?
items.a: Views aur copies ka confusing behaviour kam hota hai: chained assignment silent fail hoti hai (warning/error), aur memory copy tab banti hai jab likhna shuru karo. Isliye explicit .copy() aur .loc assignment best practice hai.

items.q: Rolling aur expanding me farq?
items.a: rolling(window=n) fixed window ka aggregate deta hai (moving average), expanding() start se ab tak ka cumulative window deta hai. Dono min_periods se control hote hain (khaali window par NaN).

items.q: idxmax aur nlargest me kab kaunsa?
items.a: idxmax() max value ka index deta hai (ek per axis); nlargest(n) top-n rows ek hi call me deta hai (grouped top-N ke liye groupby + nlargest ya sort+head).
items.x: Index chahiye → idxmax, top-N rows → nlargest.

items.q: describe() me median aur quantiles kaise milte hain?
items.a: describe() default count/mean/std/min/25/50/75/max deta hai (50% = median); custom ke liye describe(percentiles=[.9, .99]) ya quantile([0.5, 0.9]). Non-numeric columns ke liye value_counts zyada useful hai.

items.q: Grouped result ko original rows par wapas kaise laate ho (broadcast)?
items.a: transform ya map + merge: df['grp_mean'] = df.groupby('grp')['x'].transform('mean') — same index broadcast ho jaata hai, jo z-score/normalization ke liye perfect hai.
items.x: transform = group stat back on rows.

items.q: Parquet aur CSV me production me kaunsa choose karoge?
items.a: Parquet: columnar, typed, compressed, fast partial reads (columns chuno) — analytics/repeated loads ke liye better. CSV: interchange aur human-readable, par types guess hote hain aur bada file slow.

items.q: Duplicate rows ka standard treatment likho.
items.a: Pehle detect: df.duplicated(subset=[...]).sum(), phir business rule decide: exact duplicates drop, ya keep='last' (latest wins). Purge ke baad row count aur affected keys report karo.

items.q: Production pandas pipeline ko reproducible kaise rakhte ho?
items.a: Input snapshots (Parquet + hash), deterministic sorts, explicit dtypes, fixed seeds aur validation assertions (row counts, null rates, ranges) — pipeline ko code + schema version ke saath pin karo.

items.q: Real-world: outlier detection karo IQR method se aur flag column add karo (delete nahi).
items.a:
import pandas as pd

def flag_outliers(df, col, k=1.5):
    q1, q3 = df[col].quantile([0.25, 0.75])
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo, hi = q1 - k * iqr, q3 + k * iqr
    df[f'{col}_outlier'] = (df[col] < lo) | (df[col] > hi)
    return df, (lo, hi)
items.x: Flag karo, delete nahi — analyst decide karega.

items.q: Real-world: duplicate orders detect karo (same customer + same amount, 5 min window).

import pandas as pd

df = df.sort_values(['customer_id', 'created_at'])
df['delta'] = df.groupby('customer_id')['created_at'].diff()

items.q: Checkpoint: DataFrame ke chaar core inspection methods likho.
items.a: head/tail (peek), info (dtype + nulls), describe (stats), shape/columns (structure).

items.q: Checkpoint: missing value ke chaar treatment options likho.
items.a: Drop rows/columns, impute (median/mode/fill), forward/backward fill (time series), aur indicator column + impute (missingness ko feature banana).

items.q: Checkpoint: groupby ke saath teen step likho jo hamesha karte ho.
items.a: 1) groupby keys validate karo (null keys ka kya hoga). 2) agg/transform se summary nikalo. 3) result reset_index aur row count cross-check karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: merge ke chaar types aur ek-ek ka output likho.
items.a: inner (dono me match), left (left ki saari rows), right (right ki saari rows), outer (sab). Non-matching side me NaN aate hain.

items.q: Checkpoint: loc ke saath safe assignment ka pattern likho.
items.a: df.loc[df['amount'] < 0, 'amount'] = 0 — ek hi step me row filter + column + value, isliye chained-assignment ka silent fail nahi hota.

items.q: Checkpoint: datetime ke teen must-do likho.
items.a: parse_dates/errors='coerce', consistent timezone (UTC store), aur .dt accessor se components nikalna.

items.q: Checkpoint: dtypes ko explicit rakhne ke teen fayde likho.
items.a: Predictable memory, correct comparisons/sorting (string vs number), aur merge/join mismatches se bachav (int vs str key).

items.q: Checkpoint: top-N per group nikalne ka pattern likho.
items.a: df.sort_values('amount', ascending=False).groupby('group').head(3) — ya groupby('group')['amount'].nlargest(3).

items.q: Checkpoint: text cleaning ke chaar steps likho.
items.a: Type cast (astype(str)), case fold, whitespace strip, aur Unicode/punctuation normalize — tay karo kis level tak normalize karna hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: result ko validate karne ke teen assertions likho.
items.a: Row count expectation (ya delta), null rate per column, aur key uniqueness (duplicated().sum() == 0).
items.x: Asserts pipeline ko honest rakhte hain.

items.q: Checkpoint: Parquet over CSV ke teen fayde likho.
items.a: Columnar (sirf zaroori columns padho), typed (dtype guess nahi), compressed aur fast — plus schema metadata.

items.q: Checkpoint: pivot_table ke teen main parameters likho.
items.a: index (rows), columns (pivot keys), values + aggfunc (kya aggregate karna hai); saath me fill_value aur margins.

items.q: Checkpoint: pipeline ke teen reproducibility practices likho.
items.a: Input snapshot + hash, deterministic sorts/seeds, aur schema/dtype validation assertions.

items.q: Checkpoint: chained assignment ka warning message aur sahi fix likho.
items.a: SettingWithCopyWarning → fix: df.loc[mask, 'col'] = value (single step) ya pehle explicit .copy() lo.

items.q: Checkpoint: resample ke liye kya prerequisite hai?
items.a: DatetimeIndex (ya column ko DatetimeIndex banana) aur ek aggregation function; missing buckets ke liye fill_value/ffill decide karo.
items.x: Time index ke bina resample nahi.

items.q: Checkpoint: describe() non-numeric column par kya deta hai?
items.a: count, unique, top, freq (categorical summary) — numeric stats nahi. Numeric chahiye to column ko convert karo ya value_counts use karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: apply vs vectorized ka decision rule ek line me likho.
items.a: Agar operation built-in vectorized form me likha ja sakta hai (arithmetic/where/str/dt) to woh use karo; apply sirf tab jab custom per-row Python logic lazmi ho.

items.q: Checkpoint: duplicate handling ke teen steps likho.
items.a: Detect (duplicated().sum()), rule decide karo (keep first/last/aggregate), aur purge ke baad row count + affected keys log karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: groupby me dropna=False kyun zaroori ho sakta hai?
items.a: Default me null group keys drop ho jaate hain, isliye 'kitne orders me customer missing hai' jaisa sawal ka jawab gayab ho jaata hai — dropna=False se woh group dikhta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne pandas use kiya, SQL kyun nahi?'
items.a: Decision data size aur workflow par thi: data files (CSV/Parquet) aur join/feature prep par pandas fast iterate karne deta hai; jab data database me ho ya scale badhe, wahi transform SQL me chala diya jata hai. Dono jagah logic single source me rakhne ki koshish karta hoon.
items.x: Tool choice data ke location se justify karo.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare analysis me missing data ka kya effect pada — usse quantify karo.'
items.a: Missing rate 3.2% tha (mostly 'phone' column). Numeric fields par median imputation ki aur ek indicator column rakha; sensitive metric par effect compare kiya (imputation ke bina vs ke saath 1.1% difference), isliye conclusion robust tha.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare dashboard ka metric reproducible hai — koi aur wahi number nikaal sakta hai?'
items.a: Haan: definition docs me likhi hai (filters, status, date bounds), code versioned pipeline me hai with fixed dtypes/seeds, aur input snapshot hash ke saath stored hai — isliye same snapshot se same number nikalta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Outliers ko tumne delete kiya ya rakha — kyun?'
items.a: Delete nahi kiya; flag karke rakhe (IQR method) aur sensitivity analysis dikhaya: outliers ke saath mean 12% upar tha par median stable tha, isliye reporting me median + flagged view rakha. Deleting silently conclusion badal deti hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne pipeline me kaunsi validation lagayi jo production me bug pakadti hai?'
items.a: Schema + range + null assertions pipeline ke entry par: expected columns, dtype checks, amount >= 0, aur date range validation. Ek baar ek upstream column rename ne pipeline ko foran fail kiya instead of silently 0 revenue.

items.q: Project defense: 'Ek bade CSV par tumhara code kab fail hoga aur mitigation kya hai?'
items.a: Jab data RAM se bada ho jaaye (ya join me row explosion ho). Mitigation: chunked read + aggregated state, usecols aur chhote dtypes, aur bade joins ke liye DuckDB/polars. Row count sanity check har step par.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne feature engineering me leakage kaise rok'',' kya bollo?
items.a: Time-based split use kiya, target-derived features nahi banaye, aur scalers/imputers sirf training fold par fit kiye (pipeline me). Group leakage (same user train aur test me) ko bhi group split se roka.

items.q: Project defense: 'Groupby ke baad row count mismatch aaya to tum kaise debug karte ho?'
items.a: Expected vs actual rows compare karta hoon: null keys (dropna default), unexpected duplicates (validate param), aur filter order. Praktik fix: dropna=False ya key cleanup, phir merge ke saath re-verify counts.
items.x: Count mismatch = key hygiene ka sawal.

items.q: Project defense: 'Data quality ka ownership kaun karta hai — tumhara pipeline ya source team?'
items.a: Contract shared hai: source team schema promise karti hai (versioned), pipeline contract assert karti hai (fail + alert), aur mismatch par data contract discussion hoti hai. Silent coercion nahi karte — warna source team ko pata hi nahi chalega.

items.q: Project defense: 'Explain how you tuned performance — numbers ke saath.'
items.a: Profiling se pata chala 80% time ek apply call me ja raha tha. Usko str.contains + np.where vectorization me badla: 8.2s se 0.3s (27x), memory stable. Har step ke baad timing log kiya, isliye claim measurable hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare joins row count kyun badha diya aur kaise fix kiya?'
items.a: Right table me duplicate keys thi, isliye many-to-many join ne rows multiply kar diye. Fix: right side ko groupby se ek row per key banao (ya drop_duplicates with rule) aur merge me validate='many_to_one' lagao taaki ye dobara na ho.

items.q: Project defense: 'Column-level documentation kahan rakhi hai?'
items.a: Schema registry (dtype, meaning, allowed range, owner) repo me JSON/YAML me hai, aur pipeline usi se validation rules generate karta hai — docs aur code ek jagah rehte hain, isliye drift nahi hota.

items.q: Project defense: 'Ek stake holder ka number tumhare number se alag hai — kaise resolve karoge?'
items.a: Definition compare karke shuru karta hoon: date bounds, status filters, refund treatment, aur grain (orders vs customers). Phir ek chhoti reproducible example par dono queries chala kar farq dikhata hoon aur definition library me lock karta hoon.

items.q: Project defense: 'Dataset 10x bade ho jaaye to architecture kaise badloge?'
items.a: Pandas single node chhodkar DuckDB/polars (out-of-core) aur pre-aggregated tables par shift; raw data partition by date; notebook logic ko versioned jobs me convert karo with idempotent outputs aur snapshots.

items.q: Project defense: 'Agar tumhara pipeline silently galat number de de to pakadne ka mechanism kya hai?'
items.a: Metric-level monitors: row count delta, revenue distribution shift, day-over-day jump alert, aur 'as of' freshness check. Ek baar missing status filter se revenue 20% upar aa gaya tha, tab se yeh alert active hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer poochta hai tumne kya automate kiya' — jawab?
items.a: Manual Excel steps ko reproducible pipeline me convert kiya: raw → validated → aggregated daily table, jisme assertions aur alert lagte hain. Result: 4 ghante ka weekly manual work ~2 minute ka scheduled job ban gaya, aur numbers consistent.

items.q: Project defense: 'Do analysts ka farq wala number ka root cause kya nikla aur usse kya badla?'
items.a: Root cause timezone tha (ek UTC me group kar raha tha, doosra local me), isliye day boundary shift ho gayi thi. Badla: UTC store + explicit tz handling, definition docs me note, aur ek regression test jo known fixture par daily counts assert karta hai.
items.x: Silent tz bug ko test se band karo.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhara analysis kitna trustworthy hai — ek limitation batao.'
items.a: Limitation: attribution window 7 din tha, isliye long-delay conversions undercounted hain. Isliye report me method + window likha hai aur sensitivity (14/30 din window) appendix me hai — number ke saath assumption bhi bhejta hoon.

items.q: np.where aur boolean mask me kab kaunsa choose karte ho?
items.a: Mask tab jab sirf filter/summary chahiye (arr[arr > 0], mask.sum()). np.where tab jab do values me se choose karna ho (replace, clip, conditional column) — read-only selection me mask sasta aur clearer hai.

items.q: Array se top-k largest values nikalo bina poori sorting ke.
items.a:
import numpy as np

def top_k(x, k=3):
    x = np.asarray(x)
    if k >= len(x):
        return np.sort(x)[::-1]
    part = np.partition(x, -k)[-k:]
    return np.sort(part)[::-1]
items.x: partition O(n) hai, full sort O(n log n).

items.q: Do numeric columns ka correlation coefficient nikalo (numpy).
items.a:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
b = np.array([2.0, 4.0, 6.1, 8.0])
print(round(float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1]), 4))

items.q: np.array([1,2,3])[None, :].shape aur [:, None].shape — dono output batao.
items.a: (1, 3) aur (3, 1) — None se naya axis add hota hai (expand_dims ka shortcut), jo broadcasting ke liye row/column vector banata hai.

items.q: np.arange(4).reshape(2,2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=True).shape — output?
items.a: (1, 2) — axis=0 collapse hui par keepdims ne us axis ko size 1 ke roop me rakha, isliye result original ke saath broadcast ho sakta hai (normalization ke liye perfect).

items.q: Interview: 'merge me left_on/right_on aur suffixes kab use karoge?'
items.a: Jab dono tables me key column ka naam alag ho (left_on='user_id', right_on='id') aur non-key columns ka naam clash kare to suffixes=('_left', '_right') do — warna pandas silently _x/_y laga deta hai jo code me read karna confusing hota hai.

span = (orders.groupby('customer_id')['created_at']
              .agg(['min', 'max'])
              .rename(columns={'min': 'first_order', 'max': 'last_order'}))

items.q: Checkpoint: DataFrame copy karne ke teen tarike aur unka farq likho.
items.a: df (reference, wahi object), df.copy(deep=False) (naye container, par data share), df.copy() (deep, data bhi copy). Shared data par likhna original ko badal sakta hai — pandas 3 ke CoW ke baad ye behaviour safer hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare analysis code ka kaunsa hissa test kiya aur kaunsa deliberately nahi?'
items.a: Transformation functions (cleaning, aggregation, metric calc) unit tests se cover kiye chhote fixtures ke saath; plotting aur one-off exploration untested hai kyunki woh deliverable nahi. Metric layer par regression test hai jo known numbers assert karta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Data me PII column tha — tumne kaise handle kiya?'
items.a: Analysis ke liye PII drop kiya (ya hash/aggregate level tak reduce kiya) aur raw extract local machine se bahar share nahi kiya. Report me sirf aggregated numbers hain aur notebook ke cell outputs saaf kiye taaki sample PII leak na ho.
